## The 1536-Well 3-Bromopyridine Plate

**Source:** Santanilla et al., *Science* 2015, 347, 49–53 (DOI 10.1126/science.1259203)

**Plate Design:**
A 1536-well plate screening experiment examining the reactivity of **3-bromopyridine (22)** with **16 different classes of nucleophiles** under **96 Pd cross-coupling reaction conditions** — this is a 16×6 matrix of nucleophiles × bases.

**Scale & Dosing:**
- Run at **100 nanomolar scale** (extremely small)
- Reagents dosed from a 384-well plate into the 1536-well plate using a **Mosquito liquid handler** (acoustic transfer)

**Stock Concentrations Prepared:**
- Pd-precatalysts: 0.04 M in DMSO
- Aryl halide (3-bromopyridine): 0.4 M in DMSO
- Nucleophiles: 0.6 M in DMSO
- Base: 0.8 M in DMSO

**Reaction Conditions:**
- **Room temperature**, 22 hours (no heating)
- Quenched with acetic acid
- Biphenyl added as internal standard
- **UPLC** analysis

**Best Result Recorded (Well R36):**
- **Nucleophile:** 3-phenyl-1-propanol (class S9)
- **Precatalyst:** tBuBrettPhos Pd G3 (43)
- **Base:** P2Et (29)
- **Product:** 3-(3-phenylpropoxy)pyridine
- **Yield:** 29.5%
- **Note:** This was the highest-yielding real condition for this nucleophile class in the published dataset

This is a high-throughput screening plate from a major pharmaceutical optimization study on Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of 3-bromopyridine.
